title: Voyage of the Scarlet Queen
paragraphs: A serialized seafaring adventure following Captain Philip Karney, first mate Gallagher, and the crew of the Scarlet Queen through dangerous ports and Pacific intrigue.
Serialized high-seas adventure built around the ketch Scarlet Queen, Captain Philip Karney and first mate Red Gallagher.
The run breaks into several distinct periods: Mutual sustaining regular run (July 3, 1947 to February 25, 1948) on [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]].

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Elliott Lewis (performer), Edwin Max (performer), Richard Aurandt (music, performer, and composer), Charles Arlington (announcer and performer), Gil Doud (writer), Robert Tallman (writer and radio adaptor), and James Burton (producer and director).

Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]], [[org|org.cd82fd99edb39caa|Armed Forces Radio and Television Service]], [[org|org.4798d1172deaae2c|Armed Forces Radio Service]], [[org|org.50630574777d6937|Don Lee Network]], and [[org|org.87e6f64937f0bfb8|KHJ]].

The stories often return to maritime and high-seas adventure, continuing voyage and port-to-port travel, shipboard crew life and command, Pacific and Asian port settings, crime, theft and intrigue, and cargo, merchants and port commerce.

The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Postwar Pacific adventure radio, Mutual sustaining adventure programming, Maritime sound design and location realism, and 1940s American radio portrayals of Pacific and Asian locales.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include [[show|escape|Escape]], [[show|lux-radio-theatre|Lux Radio Theatre]], [[show|yours-truly-johnny-dollar|Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar]], [[show|philip-marlowe|The Adventures of Philip Marlowe]], and [[show|the-whistler|The Whistler]].
